content.title: About
content.content: Crab is a seafood product that comes from marine crustaceans of the family Portunidae and related groups. It lives in coastal waters of temperate and tropical regions. Crab meat is tender, slightly sweet, and has a distinct oceanic aroma. It is eaten raw (e.g., in sushi), boiled, baked, or as canned meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crabs can walk sideways thanks to the unique articulation of their legs.
Some crab species can change color to blend with their surroundings.
Crabs have powerful claws used for defense and for catching food.
The largest species, the Japanese spider crab (Macrocheira kaempferi), can have a leg span of up to 3.7 m.
Crabs play an important ecological role by cleaning the sea floor of dead organisms.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Crab meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other seafoods, crab is low in fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Crab is a good source of zinc, copper, selenium, and phosphorus, which aid immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Crab meat contains polyunsaturated fatty acids that promote heart health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to crab.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Crab contains cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Heavy metal contamination
items.content: Crabs from polluted waters can accumulate mercury and cadmium; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Crab is high in purines, which may exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crab meat can be used in salads, soups, pastas, rolls, and sushi. It is often boiled, steamed, or baked. Canned crab is convenient for quick dishes. Before eating, the meat should be thoroughly rinsed and the shell removed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh crab should be kept in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C and used within 2 days. Frozen crab can be stored at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Canned crab is shelf‑stable until the expiration date.
